The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy (FKF) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Medicinal Chemistry or a closely related discipline. The candidate is expected to start on 01.08.2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS, and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research, interdisciplinary exchange, active participation in DIAS and leadership activities. 

 

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of medicinal chemistry, who is eager to develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The researcher should contribute to expanding and strengthening the interface between medicinal chemistry and pharmacy at SDU, fostering interdisciplinary research and collaboration across these fields. Alongside this disciplinary focus, the successful candidate should be intellectually curious about research beyond their immediate field and motivated to participate in DIAS’s wider cross-faculty community.

 

We particularly welcome applicants whose research combines medicinal chemistry disciplines with pharmaceutical sciences, including drug delivery, formulation, biopharmaceutics, or translational drug development. We are especially interested in researchers who can establish innovative research directions that connect molecular drug design and optimization with pharmaceutical development and therapeutic translation. The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

 

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

• 
A strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Active engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

• 
The ability to communicate project results in English both in writing in academic contexts and to the broader public.

• 
The ability to teach and supervise students.

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of medicinal chemistry, chemical biology and pharmacy (to qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline). 

• 
Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

• 
Be fluent in English.

• 
Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

• 
Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

• 
Be an inspiring and engaging teacher and supervisor.

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. DIAS fellows become members of the DIAS Society of Fellows, which supports research, networking, and leadership opportunities while fostering a sense of community among early-career researchers from diverse disciplines. The Society provides guidance and support to all Fellows, ensuring they feel welcome and integrated. DIAS also offers Blue Sky Mentoring. Together, these provide support for fellows’ development and integration into the DIAS community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.  

 

The Department

At the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, we contribute to solving some of society’s greatest challenges within energy, environment, health, and sustainability. We succeed because we build bridges between disciplines and transcend traditional boundaries. Our interdisciplinary mindset is not only a fundamental condition, but also our strength. And it is a strength that ensures our research and education are recognized both nationally and internationally.

 

Our vision is to create and apply knowledge across the natural sciences. We are unique in housing research within physics, chemistry, and pharmacy under one department, which provides excellent opportunities to explore the intersections between these disciplines.

 

But we go further. At SDU, we collaborate with researchers from IMADA (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science) to advance fields towards digital transformation. We work with IGT (Department of Green Technology) and MMI (Maersk Mc-Kinney Møller Institute) to harness the potential at the intersection of research and technological application. We also collaborate with researchers from the Faculty of Health Sciences to integrate health-related perspectives.

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk. 

 

For more questions about the position please contact Head of Department Professor Jacob Kongsted, email: kongsted@sdu.dk. 

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please refer to the provided links about salary and taxation. International researchers may be eligible for the Danish Researcher Tax Scheme, which can offer favourable tax conditions. SDU can provide information and guidance regarding the scheme.

 

Danish Tenure Track Programme

An appointment as Assistant Professor (Danish tenure track) is limited to a six-year term. The academic assessment for promotion to Associate Professor must be initiated no later than the end of the fifth year of employment. However, a tenure track assistant professor may request an earlier assessment within the first four years.

If the initial assessment is negative, one reassessment may be conducted during the final six months prior to a potential transition. A maximum of two assessments may be undertaken.

A positive assessment leads to appointment to a permanent Associate Professor position. If the final assessment is negative, the employment may be terminated in accordance with the applicable collective agreement.

A six-year development plan for the tenure track programme is established at the start of employment.

 

Application requirements
The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborated research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years, including a description of synergy with the department's activities and how the applicant’s research could benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment. Applicants should also explain, in their letter of motivation, how they would contribute to DIAS’s intellectual community and engage with researchers beyond their immediate field. 

• 
Copies of certificates/Diplomas (Master and PhD degree).

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
Up to 5 of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload a pdf for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

• 
Applicants are requested to submit a teaching portfolio with the application as documentation for teaching experience as well as supervision qualifications. Formal application instructions and a guide for the teaching portfolio can be found here.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Ethics and Politics of AI Agents Postdoc position at The Digital Democracy Centre
jobs.description:
The Digital Democracy Centre (DDC) at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications for one or more full-time Postdoc positions.

The successful candidate will explore the benefits and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) agents: systems capable of planning and executing actions on behalf of users. This concerns how AI agents may transform the relationship between individuals, organisations and broader society as they become increasingly involved in decision-making, task completion and interactions with digital services. The postdoc will examine the ethical, social and political implications of the deployment of AI agents, exploring topics which could include autonomy, trust and privacy, human wellbeing, persuasion, AI value alignment and broader economic and social impacts.

The postdoc will contribute to developing an interdisciplinary understanding of these emerging technologies, drawing on relevant philosophical, social scientific and technical perspectives. The precise focus of the research will be shaped by the successful candidate’s expertise and interests.

Employment can be from May 1,  2027 or by agreement and will have a duration of up to 2 years. The place of employment will be in Odense.

Research profiles and tasks

We welcome applications from candidates with a background in one or more of the following disciplines: philosophy, computer science, sociology, political science, law and psychology. This could include philosophy of mind, action, or agency; philosophy of technology and science and technology studies; moral or political philosophy; political theory; critical political economy; critical sociology or the global governance of AI. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work engages with interdisciplinary questions and who can bring their disciplinary expertise into dialogue with other approaches. They will be embedded in an interdisciplinary team, working closely with Professor James Muldoon and collaborating with other scholars at the Centre. 

Expectations and key responsibilities

The postdoc will contribute to all stages of the research process, from the development of research questions and design through to analysis, publication and public dissemination. A strong publication record relative to career stage is expected, alongside evidence of a developing and coherent research trajectory.

Candidates are expected to be willing and able to contribute to the DDC by producing original research of high international quality; engaging with academic and non-academic audiences, including journalists, policymakers and civil society organisations; and contributing to the development of research funding proposals.

Candidates are expected to:

• 
Be capable of working independently and in a team through the research process, including with regards to data collection, data analysis, writing articles and knowledge dissemination.

• 
Contribute both academically and socially to the research environment at the DDC

• 
Be able to communicate research results in English both in writing in academic contexts and to the broader public

• 
Present research findings at international conferences 

• 
Work and be present at the Centre in Odense

Inquiries about the position can be addressed to Prof. James Muldoon (jamu@sam.sdu.dk).

About the DDC

The DDC is a part of the Faculty of Social Sciences. It is an interdisciplinary Centre with members from computer science, law, media studies, political science, business, and organization studies. The DDC believes in fostering a stimulating and inspiring environment for both faculty members and students. The DDC’s ambition is to recruit, develop, and retain talented scholars committed to both research, education, and impact. Furthermore, the DDC wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

You can find further information about the DDC HERE.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. Among other things, the staff answers questions concerning salary, taxation, housing and accompanying family. Additional information about working in Denmark can be found at Work in Denmark.

Application and assessment process

Appointment to the position requires a PhD degree or equivalent and will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the Danish state with the associated circular on the protocol on job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for the position of postdocs as described herein.

An application must include:

• 
A cover letter stating your specific interest and qualifications for the position (one page max).

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information and date entries

• 
Copies of certificates and diplomas (BSc, MSc, and PhD degrees)

• 
The names and complete contact details (including phone numbers and email addresses) of at least two references

• 
A complete list of publications indicating which publications are most relevant for the position

• 
Up to 3 of the most relevant publications or unpublished chapters of the PhD thesis. 

The application and all supporting documents must be submitted in English, with the exception of degree certificates and transcripts issued in Danish.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

Applications that are incomplete may be rejected without any substantive evaluation.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an academic assessment committee that determines whether applicants are qualified to be a postdoctoral fellow. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. The committee reserves the right to arrive at a decision solely based on the material submitted. Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The assessment report will subsequently be forwarded to the Head of Department who will assemble an appointment committee. The appointment committee will manage and complete a series of job interviews with especially promising applicants. On the basis of the applications, the written assessments, the job interviews, and a deliberation within the appointment committee, the head of department determines which candidate will be offered the position.

We recommend reading "How to apply for a position at SDU" before applying.

Application deadline: January 18, 2027, 23:59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked). The application and CV must each not exceed 10 MB in file size.

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Salary and employment terms
Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

jobs.occupation: Engineering High-Maize for Improved Mineral Bioavailability through Gene Editing and Protein Design
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Agroecology programme. The position is available from 01 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Engineering High-Phytase Maize for Improved Mineral Bioavailability through Gene Editing and Protein Design

Research area and project description
Phosphorus stored in cereal grains is largely present as phytate, a compound that strongly binds essential minerals such as iron and zinc, thereby reducing their bioavailability in food and feed. Increasing phytase activity in grain represents a promising strategy to improve mineral nutrition while reducing the environ-mental footprint of agricultural production.

The PhD project is part of the GRAINPAP initiative at Aarhus University, Department for Agroecology, Section for Crop Genetics and Biotechnology. The project aims to develop maize germplasm with enhanced mature grain phytase activity through a combination of genome editing, molecular genetics, biotechnology and computational biology.

The successful candidate will investigate members of the Purple Acid Phosphatase (PAP) gene family and apply CRISPR-based promoter engineering and gene editing approaches to increase grain-specific phytase expression. The project will furthermore explore protein engineering strategies to optimize enzyme performance and will utilize genomic and transcriptomic datasets to identify regulatory mechanisms controlling phytase accumulation in grain.

The PhD student will receive training in genome editing, molecular cloning, plant transformation, bioinformatics, functional genomics and biochemical characterization of enzymes. The project includes collaboration with leading researchers in plant biotechnology and computational genetics and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory, greenhouse and field facilities.

The position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of more nutritious and sustainable crop varieties while obtaining broad interdisciplinary skills at the interface of plant genetics, molecular biology and crop biotechnology.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant master’s degree (120 ECTS) in disciplines such as Agricultural Sciences, Molecular Biology, Plant Biotechnology, Plant Science or similar. Experience working with cereal crops, genome editing technologies, and plant transformation systems will be considered a strong advantage.

We expect that you:
 
• Have good communication skills in English, written and oral.
• Are motivated for both experimental work and scientific writing.
• Can work both independently and collaboratively
• Thrive in an informal collaborative workspace

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Agroecology, Section for Crop Genetics and Biotechnology, Research Center Flakkebjerg, Forsøgsvej 1, DK-4200 Slagelse, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the research project FanVEX: Fanization of Violent Extremism on social media at the Department of Sociology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen
jobs.description:
The Department of Sociology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the research project FanVEX: Fanization of Violent Extremism on social media to commence by 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The position is a full time fixed-term position for 30 months

  Introduction 
 Online fandom and violent extremism increasingly intersect on social media. Violent perpetrators may become objects of fandom, while extremist actors draw on fan practices and popular culture to circulate ideological messages and attract audiences (Warzel, 2025). As perpetrators and their admirers participate in digital communities and their practices overlap with mainstream fandom (Gartenstein-Ross et al., 2023; Davey & Ebner, 2017), established approaches to understanding radicalisation, motivations and the role of ideology face new challenges.

  FanVEX investigates how validation from fan communities may mobilise or accelerate violent action and which factors sustain participation in these communities. The project examines how fandom makes extremist content memetic and viral (Milner, 2016), combines ideology with popular culture (Driessen et al., 2025), and reproduces cultural scripts that can make violence appear conceivable, attractive or worthy of emulation. The aim is to advance theoretical and empirical understanding of these processes and generate insights relevant to prevention and threat assessment.

  FanVEX brings together researchers at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Sociology (MOD-Lab: Microsociology of Online Deviance) and Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics (CODEX: Copenhagen Observatory of Digital Extremism), with international partners at Malmö University and Erasmus University Rotterdam. The postdoctoral researcher will be based at the Department of Sociology and will work in close collaboration with the wider FanVEX team. Professor Jakob Demant will be the main contact for the position.

  Duties and Responsibilities
 Typically, the primary focus of a postdoctoral position will be on research. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.

  The postdoctoral researcher will contribute particularly to Work Package 4 (WP4), which asks: How does engagement with popular culture contribute to the expression of extremist ideologies? WP4 examines whether references to popular culture function as humour, imitation, motivation, or legitimisation.

  WP4 combines data-driven analyses with digital ethnography. Its quantitative component uses co-occurrence network analysis to investigate how references to popular culture relate to ideological discourse, including material from 4chan imageboards such as /pol/ and /b/ (2021–2027). It also examines changes over time through burst-detection analysis. The qualitative component studies online communities, including incels.is and Stormfront, to understand how popular culture, fandom and anti-fan practices are incorporated into extremist environments. The analyses are designed to inform one another.
 
 The postdoctoral researcher will be expected to:
 
 - Contribute to the design, collection and analysis of digital data for WP4, with particular emphasis on quantitative network and text-based analyses.
 
 - Integrate data-driven findings with digital ethnographic insights and, where relevant, qualitative interviews.
 
 - Apply rigorous research ethics and data-protection procedures when working with sensitive online material.
 
 - Collaborate across disciplinary boundaries and contribute to project meetings and research activities.
 
 - Produce both collaboratively authored and individually authored scholarly publications during the appointment.

  Qualification Requirements 
 Applicants should hold a PhD in sociology, media studies, criminology, communication, digital humanities or a closely related discipline. We seek a researcher who can work productively across qualitative and quantitative approaches and contribute to interdisciplinary publications. In assessing applications, we will place particular emphasis on:

   	
• Experience with digital ethnography and qualitative interviewing. 	
• Competence in quantitative network analysis and data-driven analysis of digital content, such as co-occurrence, sentiment or temporal analyses. 	
• Knowledge of research ethics, data protection and the responsible handling of sensitive personal data. 	
• An interest in online extremism, participatory cultures, popular culture and/or digital deviance. 	
• Strong analytical writing skills and the ability to work collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team.   You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Bekendtgørelse om stillingsstruktur for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Sociology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better. 	
• Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.   Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall research project described above. 

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, but if the Postdoc is expected to teach, then documented teaching experience can be included in the overall assessment.  

  Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the "Apply now" icon at the bottum of this page.
 The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	
• Peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 	 	 	
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 	 	   You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3. 

   	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages)   The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of the planned research contribution over the coming years. The plan should also describe your involvement in research organisation, research collaborations, and active participation in research environments at both local and international levels.

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK /approximately EUR 39,900 (5,300 EUR) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee's assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of oppertunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity ect. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen

 For additional information about the position, please contact Jakob Demant at email: jd@soc.ku.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Stimuli-Triggered Nanoparticles and T-Cell Therapeutics for Improved Treatment of Malignant Brain Tumors - DTU Health Tech
jobs.description:
If you have a strong research interest in advanced drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy and the development of innovative treatments for brain cancer, this might be the right PhD position for you.

The aim of the PhD project is to develop a novel targeted drug delivery platform for the treatment of glioblastoma. The project combines genetically engineered CAR T cells with stimuli-responsive nanoparticles and in vitro and in vivo characterization the developed platform. 

As a PhD student you will be a part of the Pharmaceutical Technology group at DTU Health Tech. Find more information at www.healthtech.dtu.dk/research/research-sections/section-idun.

In the group, we are exploring and developing targeted and advanced delivery systems to be able to e.g. deliver small molecules, biologics and vaccines. The ultimate goals of these activities are to enhance the systemic uptake, to prevent and/or cure diseases. The group is part of the Drug Delivery and Sensing (IDUN) section at DTU Department of Health Technology. Furthermore, the PhD project is in close collaboration with researchers at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), University of Copenhagen (UCPH) and Skåne University Hospital.

Responsibilities
Primarily, you will be working in the research area of nanoparticles, cancer immune therapy and brain delivery. 

The research tasks include: 

• Develop stimuli-sensitive nanoparticles and in vitro characterize these 
• Engineer CAR-T cells 
• In vitro cell characterization 
• In vivo studies to determine effect of the developed platforms.
The project will be carried out in close collaboration with colleagues from the IDUN section, SDU, UCPH and Skåne University Hospital.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate for the position will feature the following profile:

• Dynamic, independent, creative and goal-oriented
• Strong technical background in nanoparticle development
• Knowledge and hands-on experience with cell handling 
• Experience with immune therapy and in vivo studies 
• Capable of handling a multifaceted project with many stakeholders and collaborators
You are expected to have a background in areas related to pharmaceutical sciences/technology, chemistry or biomaterials. Furthermore, you are expected to be highly independent, self-motivated and enjoy collaboration in a multidisciplinary academic environment. Moreover, you should have the ability to drive the project forward and to set and achieve ambitious goals. You should also enjoy supervising and teaching BSc and MSc students. The project is highly interdisciplinary and we expect that you enjoy teamwork and are good at coordinating your work with your colleagues. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

The Healthcare sector is a globally expanding market with demands for the most advanced technological solutions. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture.
